It is inherited in autosomal recessive or autosomal dominant patterns. Sporadic cases have also been reported. It is usually diagnosed in the first year of life. Patients present with frequent and life-threatening infections.

value_new: A hereditary motor neuron disease characterized by a peripheral and cranial neuropathy, neuronal loss in anterior horns and atrophy of spinal sensory tracts, causing muscle weakness, sensory loss, diaphragmatic paralysis and respiratory insufficiency, and multiple cranial nerve deficits such as sensorineural hearing loss, bulbar symptoms, and loss of vision due to optic atrophy.

value_new: An acquired myeloproliferative disorder characterized by an elevated absolute red blood cell mass caused by uncontrolled red blood cell production, frequently associated with uncontrolled white blood cell and platelet production.

value_old: Hereditary von Willebrand disease (VWD) is a hereditary bleeding disorder caused by a genetic anomaly leading to quantitative, structural or functional abnormalities of the Willebrand factor (von Willebrand factor; VWF). Two major groups of VWF deficiency have been defined: quantitative and partial (type 1) or total (type 3), and qualitative (type 2) with several subtypes (2A, 2B, 2M, 2N).
value_new: A von Willebrand disease that is inherited and characterized by impaired primary hemostasis resulting from germline genetic variation affecting von Willebrand factor quantity, von Willebrand factor function, platelet interaction with von Willebrand factor, or related hemostatic mechanisms. It is clinically characterized by defective platelet adhesion and secondary coagulation defect that manifests as abnormal bleeding of variable severity occurring either spontaneously or in association with an invasive procedure.

value_old: A condition that is characterized by episodes of fainting (syncope) and varying degree of ventricular arrhythmia as indicated by the prolonged QT interval. The inherited forms are caused by mutation of genes encoding cardiac ion channel proteins. The two major forms are Romano-Ward syndrome (also known as long QT syndrome 1) and Jervell-Lange Nielsen syndrome.
value_new: A cardiac rhythm disease characterized by prolongation of the corrected QT (QTc) interval on the surface electrocardiogram, associated with precipitation of torsade de pointes (TdP), a polymorphic ventricular tachycardia that may cause sudden death. It is characterized by episodes of fainting (syncope) and varying degree of ventricular arrhythmia. It may be congenital or, more frequently, acquired. The inherited forms are caused by mutation of genes encoding cardiac ion channel proteins.

value_old: A malignant tumor that arises from small cutaneous nerves, is locally aggressive, and has a potential for metastasis. Characteristic histopathologic features include proliferating atypical spindle cells with slender wavy and pointed nuclei, hypocellular areas, and areas featuring organized whorls of fibroblastic proliferation. The most common primary sites are the extremities, retroperitoneum, and trunk. These tumors tend to present in childhood, often in association with neurofibromatosis 1. (From DeVita et al., Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 5th ed, p1662; Mayo Clin Proc 1990 Feb;65(2):164-72)

value_new: An adenocarcinoma that arises from glandular epithelial cells of the esophagus and the stomach, including the gastroesophageal junction.

value_old: A benign, well-circumscribed glandular neoplasm that arises from the middle ear and may exhibit neuroendocrine differentiation. It usually presents with conductive hearing loss.

value_new: A non-neoplastic inflammatory disorder of neurons.

value_old: Vaginal bleeding preceding the 20th week of gestation.

value_old: Any autosomal dominant non-syndromic intellectual disability in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the HIVEP2 gene.
value_new: Any autosomal dominant intellectual disability in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the HIVEP2 gene. Common features included neonatal complications, hypotonia, developmental delay, intellectual disability, language impairment, gastroesophageal reflux, and strabismus.

value_old: Any autosomal recessive non-syndromic intellectual disability in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the ELP2 gene.
value_new: An autosomal recessive intellectual disability caused by a variation in the ELP2 gene, reported with both non-syndromic and syndromic presentations. The syndromic presentation includes spastic diplegia, choreoathetosis and self-injurious behavior, with epilepsy, truncal hypotonia, brain atrophy, nodular heterotopia, cardiac abnormalities, coloboma and cortical visual impairment reported in some individuals.

value_old: Hereditary angioedema type 1 (HAE 1) is a form of hereditary angioedema characterized by acute edema in subcutaneous tissues, viscera and/or the upper airway.
value_new: A form of hereditary angioedema characterized by serum levels of C1NH less than 35% of normal, acute edema in subcutaneous tissues, viscera and/or the upper airway.

value_old: Hereditary angioedema type 2 (HAE 2) is a form of hereditary angioedema characterized by acute edema in subcutaneous tissues, viscera and/or the upper airway.
value_new: A form of hereditary angioedema associated with the production of a non-functional complement C1 inhibitor protein, characterized by acute edema in subcutaneous tissues, viscera and/or the upper airway.

value_old: Acquired angioedema type 2 (AAE2) is a type of acquired angioedema (AAE) characterized by acute edema in subcutaneous tissues, viscera and/or the upper airway.
value_new: An acquired angioedema (AAE) caused by malfunctioning B cells that secrete autoantibodies to the C1-INH molecule that neutralize C1-INH activity. It is often associated with dysglobulinemia of unknown origin and  characterized by acute edema in subcutaneous tissues, viscera and/or the upper airway.

value_old: Acquired angioedema type 1 (AAE 1) is a type of acquired angioedema (AAE) characterized by acute edema in subcutaneous tissues, viscera and/or the upper airway.
value_new: An acquired angioedema (AAE) often associated with lymphoproliferative or autoimmune diseases which produce immune factors that destroy C1-INH leading to low levels of C1-INH, C1q complement and C4 complement. It is characterized by acute edema in subcutaneous tissues, viscera and/or the upper airway.

value_old: A melanoma (disease) that involves the mucosa.

Primary cutaneous gamma/delta-positive T-cell lymphoma is a rare, usually aggressive, subtype of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma characterized by infiltration of the epidermis, dermis or subcutaneous tissue by a clonal population of mature, gamma/delta positive cytotoxic T-cells. Typically it presents with ulcerating plaques, tumors, or subcutaneous nodules on the skin of the extremities, however, frequent involvement of mucosal and extranodal sites (such as the nasal cavity, gastrointestinal tract or lungs) is also observed. Cases associated with panniculitis may present with hemophagocytic syndrome (abrupt onset of fever, rash, cytopenia, hepatosplenomegaly and neurological compromise). Infiltration of lymph nodes, spleen and bone marrow is uncommon and resistance to multilineage chemotherapy is reported.

A rare malignant neoplasm of the sinonasal cavity, arising from the basal layers of olfactory neuroepithelial cells in the superior nasal vault, which usually occurs in the 5th to 6th decades of life and is characterized clinically by non-specific symptoms such as progressive ipsilateral nasal block, sinusitis, facial pain, intermittent headaches, hyposmia/dysosmia, rhinorrhea and epistaxis as well as proptosis, diplopia and excessive lacrimation due to orbital extension. With early treatment and in the absence of distant metastases, ENB appears to have a good prognosis (compared to other superior nasal malignancies), despite a high rate of cervical metastases.

Maternal phenylketonuria (PKU) is a rare disorder of phenylalanine metabolism, an inborn error of amino acid metabolism, characterized by the development of microcephaly, growth retardation, congenital heart disease, facial dysmorphism and intellectual disability in nonphenylketonuric offspring of mothers with excess phenylalanine (Phe) concentrations.
value_new: A disorder of development or morphogenesis characterized by the development of microcephaly, growth retardation, congenital heart disease, facial dysmorphism and intellectual disability in nonphenylketonuric offspring of mothers with excess phenylalanine (Phe) concentrations.

value_old: Muscular pseudohypertrophy - hypothyroidism, also known as Kocher-Debre-Semelaigne syndrome is a rare disorder characterized by pseudohypertrophy of muscles due to longstanding hypothyroidism.
value_new: A rare disorder characterized by pseudohypertrophy of muscles due to longstanding hypothyroidism.

value_old: Primary pulmonary lymphoma (PPL) is a rare lymphoma of the lung, defined as a clonal lymphoid proliferation affecting one or both lungs (parenchyma and/or bronchi) in a patient with no detectable extrapulmonary involvement at diagnosis or during the subsequent 3 months. PPL comprises low grade/indolent B cell PPL forms, the most frequent form represented by the marginal B-cell lymphoma of mucosa associated lymphoid tissue (MALT lymphoma) and other non-MALT low grade lymphomas; and more rarely high-grade B-cell PPL (including diffuse large B cell lymphoma) and lymphomatoid granulomatosis (LYG).

Autosomal dominant optic atrophy and peripheral neuropathy (ADOAPN) is a form of autosomal dominant optic atrophy (ADOA), characterized by progressive and isolated visual loss in the first decade of life, decreased reflexes in the lower limbs and a mild cerebellar stance.
value_new: A hereditary optic atrophy characterized by progressive and isolated visual loss in the first decade of life, decreased reflexes in the lower limbs and a mild cerebellar stance.
A Kleefstra syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a point mutation in the EHMT1 or KMT2C gene.

value_old: Primary non-gestational choriocarcinoma of ovary is a rare ovarian germ cell malignant tumor, arising from primordial germ cells, usually presenting with nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, menstrual irregularities, and characterized by fast growth pattern, metastasis to lung, liver and brain and production of human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG). It is apparently chemoresistant and has a worse prognosis than gestational choriocarcinoma and hence should be distinguished from the latter by DNA polymorphism.

Tetrahydrobiopterin-responsive hyperphenylalaninemia/ phenylketonuria (BH4-responsive hyperphenylalaninemia/ phenylketonuria) is a form of phenylketonuria (PKU), an inborn error of amino acid metabolism, characterized by mild to moderate symptoms of PKU including impaired cognitive function, seizures, and behavioral and developmental disorders, and a marked reduction and normalization of elevated phenylalanine concentrations after oral loading with tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4; sapropterin dihydrochloride), an essential cofactor of phenylalanine hydroxylase.
value_new: A form of phenylketonuria characterized by mild to moderate symptoms of phenylketonuria including impaired cognitive function, seizures, and behavioral and developmental disorders, and a marked reduction and normalization of elevated phenylalanine concentrations after oral loading with tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4; sapropterin dihydrochloride), an essential cofactor of phenylalanine hydroxylase.

value_old: A papillary or follicular thyroid gland carcinoma with a genetic component that develops within the same family. Current studies suggest that it is inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern. It is often multifocal and bilateral and usually affects younger patients.

Hoyeraal-Hreidarsson syndrome (HHS) is a very rare X-linked recessive disorder considered to be a severe variant of dyskeratosis congenita characterized by intrauterine growth retardation, microcephaly, cerebellar hypoplasia, progressive combined immune deficiency and aplastic anemia.
value_new: A X-linked dyskeratosis congenita considered to be a severe variant of dyskeratosis congenita characterized by intrauterine growth retardation, microcephaly, cerebellar hypoplasia, progressive combined immune deficiency and aplastic anemia.

value_old: Acute myeloid leukemia with t(6;9)(p23;q34) is a rare subtype of acute myeloid leukemia with recurrent genetic abnormalities characterized by clonal proliferation of poorly differentiated myeloid blasts in the bone marrow, blood, or other tissues in patients who present the t(6;9)(p23;q34) translocation. Frequently associated with multilineage bone marrow dysplasia, it usually presents with anemia, thrombocytopenia (often pancytopenia), and other nonspecific symptoms related to ineffective hematopoesis (fatigue, bleeding and bruising, recurrent infections, bone pain) and/or extramedullary site involvement (gingivitis, splenomegaly). Basophilia, as well as poor response to chemotherapy, has been reported.

value_new: A rare genetic interstitial lung disease characterized by diffuse lung disease of variable phenotype ranging from severe respiratory insufficiency in infancy to asymptomatic adults, due to surfactant protein C deficiency. Typical presentation in infancy includes dyspnea, cough, wheezing, and gradual cyanosis, with or without failure to thrive. Radiological findings include diffuse ground-glass opacities in neonates, later interstitial thickening associated with lung hyperinflation, intraparenchymal/subpleural cysts, honeycombing, subpleural nodules, or bronchiectasis. Infiltrates and air leaks are frequent complications.
A B-cell lymphoma that is characterized by the abnormal rearrangement of two genes, MYC gene and either BCL2 or BCL6 genes.

value_old: McCune-Albright syndrome (MAS) is classically defined by the clinical triad of fibrous dysplasia of bone (FD), cafe-au-lait skin spots, and precocious puberty (PP).
value_new: A rare mosaic syndrome characterized by the combination of two or more of the following: fibrous dysplasia of bone (FD), hyperpigmented macules, and hyperfunctioning endocrinopathies (precocious puberty, hyperthyroidism, growth hormone excess, endogenous Cushing syndrome).

value_old: Bosley-Salih-Alorainy syndrome (BSAS) is characterized by variable horizontal gaze dysfunction, profound and bilateral sensorineural deafness associated commonly with severe inner ear maldevelopment, cerebrovascular anomalies (ranging from unilateral internal carotid artery hypoplasia to bilateral agenesis), cardiac malformation, developmental delay and occasionally autism. The syndrome is caused by homozygous mutations in the HOXA1 gene (7p15.2) and is transmitted in an autosomal recessive manner. The syndrome overlaps clinically and genetically with Athabaskan brain dysfunction syndrome (ABDS,). However unlike ABDS, BSAS does not manifest central hypoventilation.
value_new: A HOXA1-related syndrome that is characterized by variable horizontal gaze dysfunction, profound and bilateral sensorineural deafness associated commonly with severe inner ear maldevelopment, cerebrovascular anomalies (ranging from unilateral internal carotid artery hypoplasia to bilateral agenesis), cardiac malformation, developmental delay and occasionally autism. The syndrome is caused by homozygous mutations in the HOXA1 gene (7p15.2) and is transmitted in an autosomal recessive manner. The syndrome overlaps clinically and genetically with Athabaskan brainstem dysgenesis syndrome (ABDS). However, unlike ABDS, BSAS does not manifest central hypoventilation.

value_old: Mild phenylketonuria is a rare form of phenylketouria (PKU), an inborn error of amino acid metabolism, characterized by symptoms of PKU of mild to moderate severity.
value_new: A phenylketonuria characterized by untreated blood phenylalanine concentrations of approximately 600-1200 umol/L, intermediate between classic phenylketonuria and mild hyperphenylalaninemia, reflecting greater residual phenylalanine hydroxylase activity.

value_old: Classical phenylketonuria is a severe form of phenylketonuria (PKU) an inborn error of amino acid metabolism characterized in untreated patients by severe intellectual deficit and neuropsychiatric complications.
value_new: A phenylketonuria characterized by untreated blood phenylalanine concentrations above approximately 1200 umol/L, the most severe end of the phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency spectrum, reflecting little or no residual phenylalanine hydroxylase activity; untreated patients develop severe intellectual disability and neuropsychiatric complications.

value_old: Mild hyperphenylalaninemia (HPA) is a rare form of phenylketonuria, an inborn error of amino acid metabolism, characterized by mild symptoms of HPA.
value_new: A phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency characterized by mildly elevated untreated blood phenylalanine concentrations below the threshold at which phenylalanine-restricted dietary treatment is indicated; there is consensus that individuals with untreated blood phenylalanine below 360 umol/L should remain untreated.

value_old: Inflammatory pseudotumor (IPT) of the liver is a rare benign tumor-like lesion.
An autosomal dominant non-syndromic intellectual disability that has material basis in an autosomal dominant mutation of EHMT1 on chromosome 9q34.3.
value_new: A Kleefstra syndrome that is characterized by severe intellectual disability, hypotonia, microcephaly, epileptic seizures, flat face with hypertelorism, synophrys, anteverted nares, everted lower lip, carp mouth with macroglossia, and heart defects, and that has material basis in a microdeletion in the chromosome region 9q34.3 or a mutation in the EHMT1 gene located in that region.

value_old: An autosomal dominant hereditary condition characterized by optic atrophy and progressive visual loss.
value_new: OBSOLETE. An autosomal dominant hereditary condition characterized by optic atrophy and progressive visual loss.

value_old: Malignant dysgerminomatous germ cell tumor of ovary is the most common form of malignant germ cell tumor of ovary, arising from germ cells in the ovary, usually presenting during adolescence with pelvic mass, fever, vaginal bleeding, and acute abdomen and is characterized by bilaterality (around 10% of cases), association with dysgenetic gonads (5 to 10% of cases), elevated serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) and human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG) (in the presence of syncitiotrophoblasts). Malignant dysgerminomatous germ cell tumor of ovary responds well to chemotherapy, potentially sparing patients from infertility and early mortality.

Myxoid/round cell liposarcoma (MRCLS) is a type of liposarcoma (LS) mostly located in the limbs, with a variable behavior depending on the histological subtype. Both myxoid and round cell are distinct histological subtypes of LS.

value_new: A form of spondylodysplastic Ehlers-Danlos syndrome due to variants in B4GALT7 and characterized by short stature, variable degrees of muscle hypotonia, joint hypermobility, especially of the hands, and bowing of limbs. Additional features include the typical craniofacial gestalt (mid-face hypoplasia, round, flat face, proptosis and narrow mouth), hyperextensible skin that is soft, thin, translucent and doughy, delayed motor and/or cognitive development, characteristic radiographic findings (such as radio-ulnar synostosis, radial head subluxation or dislocation, metaphyseal flaring and osteopenia) and ocular abnormalities.

Any multiple benign circumferential skin creases on limbs in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the TUBB gene. The phenotype comprises characteristic congenital circumferential skin creases accompanied by intellectual disability, cleft palate, short stature and dysmorphic features.

Any autosomal dominant intellectual disability in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the SET gene, characterized by delayed development and intellectual disability with language delay and speech impairment. Additional features include motor delay or incoordination, minor dysmorphic features, hypotonia, hypermobility, and variable nonspecific ocular problems.

value_old: A grade I or grade II astrocytic tumor. This category includes pilocytic astrocytoma (grade I), subependymal giant cell astrocytoma (grade I), and diffuse astrocytoma (grade II).
Mild mental deficiency, short stature, macrocranium, cardiac anomalies, cutis laxa, peculiar facies, wrinkled palms and soles, small vertebral bodies

value_new: A susceptibility to the development of schwannomatosis conferred by germline mutation in the SMARCB1 gene, characterized by the onset of multiple intracranial, spinal, or peripheral schwannomas, without involvement of the vestibular nerve. Affected individuals may also have multiple meningiomas.

value_old: Any Brown-Vialetto-van Laere syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the SLC52A3 gene.
value_new: Any riboflavin transporter deficiency in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the SLC52A3 gene. It is characterized by sensorineural hearing loss and a variety of cranial nerve palsies, usually involving the motor components of the seventh and ninth to twelfth (more rarely the third, fifth, and sixth) cranial nerves. Spinal motor nerves and, less commonly, upper motor neurons are sometimes affected, giving a picture resembling amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. The onset of the disease is usually in the second decade, but earlier and later onset have been reported.

value_old: A Mendelian susceptibility or predisposition to herpes simplex infection induced encephalitis in which the cause of the diseas is a mutation in the UNC93B1 gene.
value_new: A Mendelian susceptibility or predisposition to herpes simplex infection induced encephalitis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the UNC93B1 gene.

value_old: An autosomal recessive disorder characterized by onset of recurrent viral and bacterial infections, particularly with encapsulated bacteria, and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in the first months or years of life. Immunologic workup typically shows decreased circulating B cells and hypo- or agammaglobulinemia, sometimes with neutropenia or T-cell lymphocytosis, although laboratory findings may be variable among patients. Ig replacement therapy is beneficial. Cardiac involvement can also include atrial septal defect, valvular insufficiency, and pre-excitation syndrome. Rare myopathic or neurologic involvement has been reported, but these features are not consistently part of the disorder and may be related to other genetic defects.

Any immunodeficiency in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the FNIP1 gene. Disruption of Folliculin Interacting Protein 1 alters the essential metabolic regulators AMPK and mTOR, resulting in profound B-cell deficiency, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and pre-excitation syndrome.
value_new: Any immunodeficiency in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the FNIP1 gene, characterized by onset of recurrent viral and bacterial infections, particularly with encapsulated bacteria, and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in the first months or years of life. Immunologic workup typically shows decreased circulating B cells and hypo- or agammaglobulinemia, sometimes with neutropenia or T-cell lymphocytosis, although laboratory findings may be variable among patients. Ig replacement therapy is beneficial. Cardiac involvement can also include atrial septal defect, valvular insufficiency, and pre-excitation syndrome. Rare myopathic or neurologic involvement has been reported, but these features are not consistently part of the disorder and may be related to other genetic defects. Disruption of Folliculin Interacting Protein 1 alters the essential metabolic regulators AMPK and mTOR, resulting in profound B-cell deficiency, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and pre-excitation syndrome.

Any neurodevelopmental disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the CIC gene. It is characterized by intellectual disability, global developmental delay, seizures, autism spectrum disorder and attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder, with a spectrum that extends to isolated epilepsy.

Any autosomal dominant intellectual disability in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the NAA15 gene. It presents with a wide array of manifestations that affect the heart, brain, musculoskeletal system, and behavioral and cognitive development.

Any autosomal dominant intellectual disability in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the KMT5B gene. It is associated with global developmental delay, macrocephaly, autism, seizures, and congenital anomalies, with hypotonia and congenital heart defects as prominent features.

Any neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the CLCN6 gene. It is characterized by severe global developmental delay apparent in infancy or early childhood. Affected individuals have hypotonia with impaired motor development, respiratory insufficiency, and feeding difficulties requiring intervention. Intellectual and speech development is also delayed, and most have visual defects, including cortical visual blindness, nystagmus, and esotropia. The disorder is progressive, as manifest by developmental regression consistent with neurodegeneration.

An inherited platelet-type bleeding disorder caused by heterozygous variants in the ITGB3 gene that alter integrin alpha-IIb/beta-3 inside-out and outside-in signaling, resulting in defective platelet production and function. Affected individuals present with congenital macrothrombocytopenia, comprising mild to moderate thrombocytopenia, giant platelets and platelet anisocytosis, together with variable mucocutaneous bleeding. Functional studies show reduced integrin alpha-IIb/beta-3 expression or impaired activation, decreased platelet aggregation in response to physiologic agonists, and impaired platelet spreading on fibrinogen.

A syndromic disease caused by a variation in the COPB1 gene, characterized by severe intellectual disability, global developmental delay with absent or limited speech, inability or difficulty to walk, early-onset cataract, and variable microcephaly. Additional features may include dysmorphic facial features, hypotonia, spasticity, metabolic abnormalities, and immunodeficiency with lymphopenia.

An inborn error of immunity caused by variants in the RELA gene that cause decreased RELA (NF-kB p65) protein function. The disease is characterized by chronic mucocutaneous ulcerations, variable immune deficiency, lymphoproliferation with autoimmune cytopenias, inflammatory bowel disease, and autoinflammatory manifestations such as recurrent fever and arthralgia. Affected Individuals express various combinations of clinical features.

Any combined immunodeficiency in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the IL7 gene. It is characterized mainly by the onset of warts and verrucous or plaque-like skin lesions associated with HPV infection. There is an increased risk of skin malignancy. Some patients may have other symptoms of immune dysfunction, including mycobacterial, herpes simplex virus (HSV), or fungal infections.

A severe autosomal recessive neurodevelopmental disorder with progressive microcephaly, and high prevalence of cortical malformations, specifically polymicrogyria, and high prevalence of epilepsy and spasticity.

An erythrokeratodermia variabilis caused by a variation in the KDSR gene, which impairs the sphingolipid pathway enzyme 3-ketodihydrosphingosine reductase. Affected individuals develop severe localized and acral hyperkeratotic, erythematous and scaly plaques, particularly on the face, genitals, hands and feet. Some individuals also exhibit thrombocytopenia or abnormal platelet production, reflecting the role of sphingolipid metabolism in megakaryocyte maturation.

value_old: OBSOLETE. A rare systemic disease for which two subtypes exist, either related to the gene PLOD1 or FKBP14 (formerly FKBP22), and for which the clinically overlapping characteristics include congenital muscle hypotonia, congenital or early-onset kyphoscoliosis (progressive or non-progressive), and generalized joint hypermobility with dislocations/subluxations (in particular of the shoulders, hips, and knees). Additional features which may occur in both subtypes are skin hyperextensibility, easy bruising of the skin, rupture/aneurysm of a medium-sized artery, osteopenia/osteoporosis, blue sclerae, umbilical or inguinal hernia, chest deformity, marfanoid habitus, talipes equinovarus, and refractive errors. Gene-specific features, with variable presentation, are additionally observed in each subtype.

A rare genetic autoinflammatory syndrome with immune deficiency characterized by a combination of autoinflammation, immunodeficiency, and neutrophil dysfunction, as well as mild bleeding diathesis. Patients present recurrent attacks of abdominal pain, high fever, and systemic inflammation lasting four to five days and occurring every few weeks. Attacks may be accompanied by nailbed, tongue, submandibular, and gluteal abscesses, intra-abdominal granulomas, pyoderma gangrenosum, and buccal ulcerations. Frequent episodes of purulent paronychia, superficial skin and mucosal infections, and purulent upper respiratory tract infections have also been reported.

A rare genetic cerebral small vessel disease characterized by an adult-onset primary microangiopathy with severe atherosclerosis of arterioles and secondary leukoencephalopathy. Patients may present with migraine, transient ischemic attacks, stroke with central facial palsy, cognitive dysfunction with impaired concentration, dementia, depression, movement disorder, vertigo, dysphagia, dysarthria, sicca syndrome, impaired REM sleep, and therapy-resistant hypertension, among others. Brain MRI typically shows a leukoencephalopathy that is disproportionately severe and extensive compared to the clinical disease.

value_new: A rare genetic cerebral small vessel disease characterized by an adult-onset primary microangiopathy with severe atherosclerosis of arterioles and secondary leukoencephalopathy. Patients may present with migraine, transient ischemic attacks, stroke with central facial palsy, cognitive dysfunction with impaired concentration, dementia, depression, movement disorder, vertigo, dysphagia, dysarthria, sicca syndrome, impaired REM sleep, and therapy-resistant hypertension, among others. Brain MRI typically shows a leukoencephalopathy that is disproportionately severe and extensive compared to the clinical disease.

value_old: An acute myeloid leukemia with mutation of the nucleophosmin gene. It is usually associated with normal karyotype and frequently has myelomonocytic or monocytic features. It usually responds to induction therapy.

value_new: Any Kleefstra syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the KMT2C gene, characterized by delayed psychomotor development, variably impaired intellectual development, and mild dysmorphic features.

A multiple congenital anomalies/dysmorphic syndrome caused by heterozygous germline gain-of-function variants in the ABL1 gene that increase ABL1 kinase activity. It is characterized by congenital heart disease, skeletal and joint abnormalities (including pectus excavatum, scoliosis, and hyperextensibility or contractures of the finger joints), variable dysmorphic facial features, and failure to thrive. It is allelic to, but distinct from, human ABL1 deficiency syndrome, which is caused by homozygous loss-of-function variants in ABL1.

value_old: An autosomal dominant hereditary syndrome caused by germline pathogenic POLD1 variants. It is characterized by the presence of colorectal polyps and colorectal cancer.
A progressive bulbar palsy of childhood that occurs during childhood.
value_new: A progressive bulbar palsy that occurs during childhood and presents with hypotonia and respiratory insufficiency.

value_old: A platelet disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variant in the TPM4 gene.
value_new: A platelet disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variant in the TPM4 gene which encodes tropomyosin‑4, a key actin‑binding protein required for cytoskeletal stability during megakaryocyte maturation and platelet formation. Affected individuals show macrothrombocytopenia or normal platelet counts with enlarged platelets, often accompanied by variable platelet functional defects including impaired spreading on fibrinogen, reduced formation of filopodia and lamellipodia, decreased granule content, and vacuolated platelets. Clinical manifestations include easy bruising, epistaxis, gum bleeding, menorrhagia, and bleeding after surgery or tooth extraction; however, some mutation carriers are minimally symptomatic or asymptomatic.

value_old: Any Mendelian disease in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the TRAF3 gene. TRAF3 haploinsufficiency caused by heterozygous loss of function (null) variants presents as an immune dysregulation syndrome of recurrent bacterial infections, autoimmunity, systemic inflammation, B cell lymphoproliferation, and hypergammaglobulinemia.
value_new: An  immunodeficiency disease caused a variation in the TRAF3 gene. TRAF3 haploinsufficiency caused by heterozygous loss of function (null) variants presents as an immune dysregulation syndrome of recurrent bacterial infections, autoimmunity, systemic inflammation, B cell lymphoproliferation, and hypergammaglobulinemia.

value_old: A newly discovered disorder caused by a change (variant or mutation) in the TCF7L2 gene. This mutation may be responsible for developmental delays in childhood, intellectual disability, autism, myopia, ADHD, abnormal physical features and other problems. There is a wide spectrum of severity for individuals affected with TRND. Many of the symptoms of TRND overlap with other neurodevelopmental disorders. TRND must be diagnosed with a genetic test and cannot be diagnosed by symptoms alone.
value_new: A neurodevelopmental disorder caused by a variation in the TCF7L2 gene. This disorder is characterised by speech delay, craniofacial dysmorphism, ophthalmologic conditions including myopia, autism, intellectual disability, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, and orthopaedic abnormalities. Phenotypic severity is variable and does not cluster by variant type or genomic locus.

value_old: A non-severe combined immunodeficiency caused by a loss-of-function variation in the IKZF2 gene that is characterized by recurrent upper respiratory infections, thrush and mucosal ulcers, and chronic lymphadenopathy.
value_new: An inborn error of immunity caused by a loss-of-function variation in the IKZF2 gene that is characterized by recurrent upper respiratory infections and chronic fungal or viral infections often associated with lymphopenia and hypogammaglobulinemia. Other patients present with features of a primary immune regulatory disorder (PIRD), including autoimmunity, autoinflammation, lymphoproliferation, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), and EBV-associated hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH).
Any congenital myopathy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the TPM3 gene, and has autosomal dominant inheritance.

value_old: A cell type cancer that is composed of epithelial tissue in which tumor cells form glands or glandlike structures, representing an early form of colorectal cancer.
A bladder carcinoma that is characterized as an undifferentiated neoplasm composed of primitive-appearing cells.
A B-cell lymphoma that is characterized by the abnormal rearrangement of two genes, MYC gene and either BCL2 or BCL6 genes.
An acute myeloid leukemia typically showing megakaryocytic maturation and associated with t(1;22)(p13;q13), resulting in the expression of RBM15-MKL1 fusion protein.

value_new: Any amyotrophic lateral sclerosis in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the SPTLC1 gene.

Any inherited thrombocytopenia in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the GALE gene. It is characterized by lifelong severe macrothrombocytopenia with giant or grey platelets, bleeding diathesis, intellectual disability, mitral valve prolapse, and jaundice, with B-cell lymphopenia, low IgA and IgM, impaired specific antibody responses, and recurrent viral respiratory infections.

An autosomal recessive congenital dyserythropoietic anemia in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the KLF1 gene, characterized by neonatal jaundice, hyperbilirubinemia, and severe congenital hemolytic anemia requiring transfusion.
